newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt announces first IT outsource group.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt announces first IT outsource group.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it was seeking tenders for the management of some government agencies' information technology needs.
Finance Minister John Fahey said the group of government agencies was the first of several whose information technology services would be outsourced.

The first group, known as Cluster 3, included the Administrative Services Department, Immigration Department, the Australian Securities Commission, the Australian Electoral Commission and the Australian Industrial Property Organisation.

"Through this outsourcing initiative, the government is committed to achieving the best value for its information technology dollar, to support the delivery of services at the lowest cost to the taxpayer," Fahey said in a statement.
Fahey said the Cluster 3 group was conservatively valued at around A$250 million over a five-year period.
"This initiative creates substantial opportunities for small to medium sized Australian IT companies, regional development and employment growth," he said.
"The ability to ensure these objectives are realised will be a major component in the competitive process for this cluster and future clusters."
Fahey said companies had been invited to register their interest in the cluster and a draft request for tenders would be released in early September.
A final request for tenders would be released about five weeks later with the process expected to be finalised in April 1998.
The government announced its intention to outsource its information technology needs in its 1997/98 budget, saying it aimed to save A$38.1 million in the year to June 30, 1998.
The savings were forecast to rise to A$103.5 million a year by 2000/01.
